{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  # Apart from the Node version-file check, none of these depend on the Node version or on a build, so
  # they run once in their own job rather than on one leg of the build matrix: a failure reports on its own instead of cancelling the other
  # legs and withholding every build result. `cs-check` runs ahead of `lint` so the one
  # failure that has an automatic fix is never hidden behind the slowest step.
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      # The deploy job runs only on main and takes its artifacts from the build leg matching `.nvmrc`, so a `.nvmrc`
      # no build leg lists would pass every PR and fail only after merge. This runs before `setup-node`, which would
      # accept `v26` or `lts/*`. Netlify's `NODE_VERSION` outranks `.nvmrc`, and nodenv reads only `.node-version`.
      - name: Check the Node version files agree with the build matrix
        run: |
          v=$(tr -d '\r' < .nvmrc)
          [[ $v =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "::error::.nvmrc ($v) is not a bare major"; exit 1; }
          yq '.jobs.build.strategy.matrix."node-version"[]' .github/workflows/ci.yml | grep -qx "$v.x" || { echo "::error::no build matrix leg is $v.x, the .nvmrc version"; exit 1; }
          [ "$(tr -d '\r' < .node-version)" = "$v" ] || { echo "::error::.node-version doesn't match .nvmrc ($v)"; exit 1; }
          grep -qE "^ *NODE_VERSION = \"$v\"" netlify.toml || { echo "::error::netlify.toml's NODE_VERSION doesn't match .nvmrc ($v)"; exit 1; }
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
        with:
          run_install: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version-file: '.nvmrc'
          cache: 'pnpm'
          cache-dependency-path: 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm dedupe --check
      - run: pnpm run cs-check
      - run: pnpm run lint
      - run: pnpm run knip

  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [22.x, 24.x, 26.x]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
        with:
          run_install: false
      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: 'pnpm'
          cache-dependency-path: 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # `checks` verifies that a leg matches `.nvmrc`.
      - name: Read the deploy Node version
        id: nvmrc
        run: echo "node-version=$(tr -d '\r' < .nvmrc).x" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build with Netlify badge
        run: pnpm run build-serial
        env:
          VITE_SHOW_NETLIFY_BADGE: true
          NODE_OPTIONS: --max_old_space_size=4096

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm run build-serial
        env:
          NODE_OPTIONS: --max_old_space_size=4096

      - name: Check the build kept each 'use client' directive
        run: node scripts/checkUseClientBuild.mts

      - if: matrix.node-version == steps.nvmrc.outputs.node-version
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: playground
          path: packages/playground/dist
      - if: matrix.node-version == steps.nvmrc.outputs.node-version
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: docs
          path: packages/docs/build

  # Tests resolve `@rjsf/*` to source, so they need no build and run beside the build job. They are split across two
  # runners because nx's `--parallel` can't add CPU: each vitest run already starts a worker per core, so more tasks on
  # one runner only slow each test. The themes, which take most of the time, run on one runner. Everything else, any
  # new package included, runs on the other, along with bootstrap3 to even them out.
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node-version: [22.x, 24.x, 26.x]
        shard: [themes, others]
        include:
          - shard: themes
            nx-filter: --projects
          - shard: others
            nx-filter: --exclude

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
        with:
          run_install: false
      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: 'pnpm'
          cache-dependency-path: 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm test ${{ matrix.nx-filter }}="$THEMES"
        env:
          THEMES: '@rjsf/antd,@rjsf/chakra-ui,@rjsf/daisyui,@rjsf/fluentui-rc,@rjsf/mantine,@rjsf/mui,@rjsf/react-bootstrap,@rjsf/shadcn'

  deploy_playground_and_docs:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    name: Deploy playground and docs to GitHub Pages
    needs: [build, test, checks]
    steps:
      - name: Download built playground
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: playground
          path: dist
      - name: Download built docs
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: docs
          path: dist/docs
      - name: Deploy playground + docs to GitHub Pages
        uses: crazy-max/ghaction-github-pages@v5.0.0
        with:
          keep_history: true
          target_branch: gh-pages
          build_dir: dist
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}",
  "rationale": "The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by the measured experiment example batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508, which added timeout-minutes to a checks job and preserved all successful conclusions while reducing elapsed time. The repository's CI history shows representative successful-duration history (successful runs completing in roughly 6-8 minutes), satisfying the pattern precondition, and adding a timeout only bounds runaway consumption without removing any build/test step or changing required checks. I applied a 10-minute timeout to the checks job, which is above the checks portion of observed runs so valid slow runs are not cut off (respecting the contraindication that valid slow runs must not exceed the limit), while capping runaway jobs. No permissions, secrets, deployment, or new network access is introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
